title: KV cache offload to host memory
design_ref: KV cache offload: a second tier for prefixes that no longer fit in GPU memory
purpose: Give three single-GPU servers a host-memory tier of 0, 8 and 24 GiB (plus an unchanged control), drive them with a code-heavy mix whose repositories do not fit in GPU memory together, and read how much the second tier served, what it cost, and whether code requests got their first token sooner.

checks.description: all four servers start (the offload tiers are allocated in pinned host memory at start)
checks.because: base 124.9 s; control 1.2 s; off8 12.5 s; off24 1.2 s

checks.description: the servers with a host tier report tokens served from it and bytes moved over PCIe; the servers without report none
checks.because: The connector's own counters: external prefix-cache hits and total offloaded bytes. A tier that was configured but never read would show zero here.

checks.description: a bigger host tier serves more of the prompt: the share found in the host tier grows from 8 GiB to 24 GiB
checks.because: Host-tier share 27% at 8 GiB, 39% at 24 GiB. 8 GiB holds about 58,000 tokens of this model's KV cache and 24 GiB about 175,000; the 48 repositories need about 57,000.

checks.description: with a host tier, a larger share of all prompt tokens is found without recomputing them than on the server without one
checks.because: Found in GPU or host memory: 33% (base), 34% (control), 62% (8 GiB), 74% (24 GiB).

notes: Capacity per GPU: base 0.31, control 0.31 (noise 0.00), 8 GiB 0.32, 24 GiB 0.32 req/s. The host tier did not raise capacity by more than the noise on this traffic: the copies and the T4's compute, not the lost prefixes, set the limit.
